subject: RELEASE statement
notes: kb/Work PB348 LANDED. RULE (`--check 14.9.32.3 "Literal-1 shall not be a zero-length literal."` => OK). WHAT WAS ABSENT: the length test -- WriteSource routed literal-1 straight to host.Expr.LiteralOperand with no inspection. It was a missing APPLICATION, not a missing capability: the same BoundStringLiteral { Value.Length: 0 } predicate is applied in ControlFlowBinder (the STOP RUN / GOBACK status literal, COBOL1704), IntrinsicBinder, DataBinder.Switches and CallBinder, and the premise was proved rather than assumed -- `STOP RUN WITH ERROR STATUS "".` is rejected, so the compiler both lexes and models "" as a zero-length literal. WHAT IS THERE NOW: the rule rides the RELEASE row of FromPhraseRules and is applied by BindFromPhrase, diagnostic COBOL1915. It is RELEASE's rule ALONE -- neither 14.9.51.3 nor 14.9.35.3 states it for the FROM phrase -- which is why the rules table carries it as a nullable clause per verb rather than a screen every FROM phrase pays. The 1985 leg is outside the golden's reject-at header: at X3.23-1985 the FROM phrase admits only identifier-1, so a literal sender is refused by COBOL0871 before SR4 is reached. || EDITIONS AS ADJUDICATED: 2002 . 2014 . 2023
